content: load skills: /load-project-context, write-tests and tdd. ToolParts carries the same payload three ways (content, output_text, input_data), and the JSON path sidesteps that by shortening one structured dict in a single call. Unifying the colored and XML paths onto one structured representation would let shortening happen once. For grounding: ToolParts is a NamedTuple in src/chats/parts.py, built by tool_to_parts in src/chats/tools.py, and it‚s the single normalized handoff between tool parsing and tool rendering. The duplication exists because there are two rendering targets with different needs: the XML/raw/LLM-piping path (render_tool_xml in src/chats/formatting.py) consumes the flat, fence-wrapped content string, while the colored terminal path (render_tool_rich / _tool_body_renderable, same file) ignores content and instead reaches for the structured raw fields ‚Äî input_data to draw an Edit as a unified diff, output_text to syntax-highlight a Read result by file extension. The JSON path is the odd one out and the hint at the better design: it never touches ToolParts at all, going through tool_to_json + a single shorten_data(tool_json) call (src/chats/model.py), which is why it has none of this problem. The reason this is a real but non-trivial seam ‚Äî not a free cleanup ‚Äî is a constraint that bit a recent shortening bug: truncate_middle shortens by character count, and content bakes the code-fence/old_string:/new_string: scaffolding into the string before shortening, so you cannot simply shorten the raw payload at the source and re-wrap it without changing the exact bytes of the XML output, which is pinned by a golden-reference test (tests/). Any unification must therefore preserve current observable output across all of XML, raw, colored, and JSON while collapsing the three-way representation down to one structured source that each renderer formats on its own terms.

1	from __future__ import annotations
2	
3	import json
4	
5	from .parts import ToolParts
6	from .registry import TOOL_SCHEMAS, ContentBlockType
7	from .utils import extract_text_from_content, shorten_tool_use_id
8	
9	
10	def _format_edit_content(input_data: dict) -> str:
11	    """Format Edit tool content with old_string/new_string blocks."""
12	    parts = []
13	    if old_string := input_data.get("old_string", ""):
14	        parts.append(f"old_string:\n```\n{old_string}\n```")
15	    if new_string := input_data.get("new_string", ""):
16	        parts.append(f"new_string:\n```\n{new_string}\n```")
17	    return "\n".join(parts)
18	
19	
20	def tool_to_parts(tool: dict, id_map: dict[str, str] | None = None) -> ToolParts:
21	    """Convert a raw tool dict to normalized ToolParts.
22	
23	    Contains ALL tool formatting decisions:
24	    - TOOL_SCHEMAS attribute extraction
25	    - Edit tool special-casing
26	    - Unknown tool JSON fallback
27	    - tool_result formatting
28	    """
29	    tool_type = tool.get("type", "")
30	    input_tag = ContentBlockType.TOOL_INPUT.value.xml_tag
31	    output_tag = ContentBlockType.TOOL_OUTPUT.value.xml_tag
32	
33	    if tool_type == "tool_use":
34	        return _tool_use_to_parts(tool, input_tag)
35	
36	    if tool_type == "tool_result":
37	        return _tool_result_to_parts(tool, output_tag, id_map)
38	
39	    # Unknown type: fallback to JSON dump
40	    return ToolParts(
41	        tag=input_tag,
42	        attrs=[("name", "Unknown")],
43	        content=f"```json\n{json.dumps(tool, indent=2)}\n```",
44	        is_empty=False,
45	    )
46	
47	
48	def tool_to_json(
49	    tool: dict,
50	    id_map: dict[str, str] | None = None,
51	) -> dict[str, object]:
52	    """Convert a raw tool dict to structured JSON-friendly data."""
53	    tool_type = tool.get("type", "")
54	    input_tag = ContentBlockType.TOOL_INPUT.value.xml_tag
55	    output_tag = ContentBlockType.TOOL_OUTPUT.value.xml_tag
56	
57	    if tool_type == "tool_use":
58	        return _tool_use_to_json(tool, input_tag)
59	
60	    if tool_type == "tool_result":
61	        return _tool_result_to_json(tool, output_tag, id_map)
62	
63	    return {
64	        "type": input_tag,
65	        "name": "Unknown",
66	        "content": tool,
67	    }
68	
69	
70	def _tool_use_to_parts(tool: dict, tag: str) -> ToolParts:
71	    """Convert tool_use to ToolParts."""
72	    name = tool.get("name", "Unknown")
73	    input_data = tool.get("input", {})
74	    schema = TOOL_SCHEMAS.get(name)
75	
76	    attrs: list[tuple[str, str]] = [("name", name)]
77	    if short_tool_id := shorten_tool_use_id(tool.get("id")):
78	        attrs.append(("id", short_tool_id))
79	
80	    content: str | None = None
81	
82	    if schema:
83	        for key in schema.attr_keys:
84	            if val := input_data.get(key):
85	                attrs.append((key, str(val)))
86	
87	        if name == "Edit":
88	            content = _format_edit_content(input_data)
89	        elif schema.content_key and (val := input_data.get(schema.content_key)):
90	            lang = schema.content_lang or ""
91	            content = f"```{lang}\n{val}\n```"
92	    elif input_data:
93	        content = f"```json\n{json.dumps(input_data, indent=2)}\n```"
94	
95	    return ToolParts(
96	        tag=tag,
97	        attrs=attrs,
98	        content=content,
99	        is_empty=not content,
100	        name=name,
101	        input_data=input_data if isinstance(input_data, dict) else None,
102	        tool_use_id=tool.get("id"),
103	    )
104	
105	
106	def _tool_use_to_json(tool: dict, tag: str) -> dict[str, object]:
107	    """Convert tool_use to structured JSON data."""
108	    payload: dict[str, object] = {
109	        "type": tag,
110	        "name": tool.get("name", "Unknown"),
111	    }
112	    if short_tool_id := shorten_tool_use_id(tool.get("id")):
113	        payload["id"] = short_tool_id
114	
115	    input_data = tool.get("input", {})
116	    if not input_data:
117	        return payload
118	    if not isinstance(input_data, dict):
119	        payload["content"] = input_data
120	        return payload
121	
122	    conflicting_keys = set(payload).intersection(input_data)
123	    if conflicting_keys:
124	        payload["input"] = input_data
125	        return payload
126	
127	    payload.update(input_data)
128	    return payload
129	
130	
131	def _tool_result_to_parts(
132	    tool: dict, tag: str, id_map: dict[str, str] | None = None
133	) -> ToolParts:
134	    """Convert tool_result to ToolParts."""
135	    content_text = "\n".join(extract_text_from_content(tool.get("content", "")))
136	    is_error = tool.get("is_error", False)
137	    tool_use_id = tool.get("tool_use_id")
138	
139	    name = id_map.get(tool_use_id, "") if id_map and tool_use_id else ""
140	    attrs: list[tuple[str, str]] = []
141	    if name:
142	        attrs.append(("name", name))
143	    if short_tool_id := shorten_tool_use_id(tool_use_id):
144	        attrs.append(("id", short_tool_id))
145	    if is_error:
146	        attrs.append(("is_error", "true"))
147	
148	    content = f"```\n{content_text}\n```" if content_text else None
149	
150	    return ToolParts(
151	        tag=tag,
152	        attrs=attrs,
153	        content=content,
154	        is_empty=not content,
155	        name=name,
156	        output_text=content_text or None,
157	        tool_use_id=tool_use_id,
158	    )
159	
160	
161	def _tool_result_to_json(
162	    tool: dict,
163	    tag: str,
164	    id_map: dict[str, str] | None = None,
165	) -> dict[str, object]:
166	    """Convert tool_result to structured JSON data."""
167	    payload: dict[str, object] = {"type": tag}
168	    tool_use_id = tool.get("tool_use_id")
169	    if id_map and tool_use_id and (name := id_map.get(tool_use_id)):
170	        payload["name"] = name
171	    if short_tool_id := shorten_tool_use_id(tool_use_id):
172	        payload["id"] = short_tool_id
173	    if tool.get("is_error", False):
174	        payload["is_error"] = True
175	    if "content" in tool:
176	        payload["content"] = tool.get("content")
177	    return payload
178	
179	
180	def render_tool_xml(parts: ToolParts) -> str:
181	    """Render ToolParts to XML string."""
182	    attr_str = " ".join(f'{k}="{v}"' for k, v in parts.attrs)
183	    tag_open = f"<{parts.tag} {attr_str}>" if attr_str else f"<{parts.tag}>"
184	
185	    if parts.is_empty:
186	        return f"{tag_open}</{parts.tag}>"
187	    return f"{tag_open}\n{parts.content}\n</{parts.tag}>"

231	        if self.subagent_task:

407	    def _tool_name_id_map(
408	        self,
409	        filter_value: bool | list[ToolFilter],
410	        tool_id_map: dict[str, str] | None,
411	    ) -> dict[str, str]:
412	        """Return a tool id map, building a local one only when needed."""
413	        id_map = tool_id_map or {}
414	        if not (
415	            isinstance(filter_value, list)
416	            and not tool_id_map
417	            and any(filter_item.name is not None for filter_item in filter_value)
418	        ):
419	            return id_map
420	
421	        for tool in self.tools:
422	            if tool.get("type") == "tool_use" and "id" in tool:
423	                id_map[tool["id"]] = tool.get("name", "Unknown")

441	    def get_wrapper_type(self) -> ContentBlockType:
442	        """Return the XML wrapper type for this message.
443	
444	        agent_id takes precedence over role so that every message belonging to a
445	        subagent (including its tool-result `user` entries) renders as one block.
446	        """
447	        if self.wrapper_type is not None:
448	            return self.wrapper_type
449	        if self.agent_id:
450	            return ContentBlockType.AGENT
451	        if self.role == "user":
452	            return ContentBlockType.USER_MESSAGE
453	        if self.role == "session-rename":
454	            return ContentBlockType.SESSION_RENAME
455	        return ContentBlockType.ASSISTANT_RESPONSE

457	    def get_header(self) -> str | None:
458	        """Return the wrapper header, enriched with the subagent nickname when present.
459	
460	        A user-initiated `/fork` (subagent_type "fork") is labelled `Fork` to set it
461	        apart from agent-initiated `Task` subagents, which stay `Agent`.
462	        """
463	        wrapper = self.get_wrapper_type()
464	        header = wrapper.value.header
465	        if wrapper is not ContentBlockType.AGENT:
466	            return header
467	        if self.subagent_type == "fork":
468	            return "## Fork"
469	        if self.name:
470	            return f"{header} '{self.name}'"
471	        return header

473	    def get_date_attribute(self) -> str | None:
474	        """Return the message date for XML attributes."""
475	        if timestamp := _message_timestamp_datetime(self.timestamp):
476	            return timestamp.date().isoformat()
477	        return None

479	    def get_display_date(self) -> str | None:
480	        """Return the message date for Rich panel titles."""
481	        timestamp = _message_timestamp_datetime(self.timestamp)
482	        if timestamp is None:
483	            return None
484	        return f"{timestamp:%B} {_ordinal_day(timestamp.day)}"

486	    def get_wrapper_attrs(self) -> str:
487	        """Build XML attributes string for this message's wrapper tag."""
488	        attrs = [f'i="{self.index}"']
489	        if self.branch_id:
490	            attrs.append(f'branch="{self.branch_id}"')
491	        if self.role == "user":
492	            if self.is_meta:
493	                attrs.append('isMeta="true"')
494	            if self.source_tool_user_id:
495	                attrs.append(f'sourceToolUserId="{self.source_tool_user_id}"')
496	        if self.agent_id:
497	            attrs.append(f'agent_id="{self.agent_id}"')
498	            if self.subagent_type:

500	            if self.name:

502	        if self.model:

504	        if date := self.get_date_attribute():
505	            attrs.append(f'date="{date}"')
506	        return " ".join(attrs)

43	class HighlightedMarkdown:
44	    """Render Markdown, then re-style substrings matching a regex (search hits).
45	
46	    Works on the rendered segment stream rather than reaching into Rich's
47	    Markdown internals, so the term highlight survives full markdown formatting
48	    and the renderable still wraps/sizes itself inside a Panel. Matches that fall
49	    within one rendered run — the common case for a search term — are
50	    highlighted; a term split across a style boundary is left untouched.
51	    """
52	
53	    def __init__(self, markup: str, regex: re.Pattern[str], style: str) -> None:
54	        self.markup = markup
55	        self.regex = regex
56	        self.style_name = style
57	
58	    def __rich_console__(
59	        self, console: Console, options: ConsoleOptions
60	    ) -> RenderResult:
61	        highlight = console.get_style(self.style_name)
62	        for text, style, control in console.render(Markdown(self.markup), options):
63	            if control is not None or not text or not self.regex.search(text):
64	                yield Segment(text, style, control)
65	                continue
66	            cursor = 0
67	            for match in self.regex.finditer(text):
68	                if match.start() > cursor:
69	                    yield Segment(text[cursor : match.start()], style, control)
70	                combined = style + highlight if style else highlight
71	                yield Segment(match.group(), combined, control)
72	                cursor = match.end()
73	            if cursor < len(text):
74	                yield Segment(text[cursor:], style, control)
75

77	def _text_renderable(markup: str, highlight_regex: re.Pattern[str] | None):
78	    """Return a Markdown renderable, highlighting search terms when asked."""
79	    if highlight_regex is None:
80	        return Markdown(markup)
81	    return HighlightedMarkdown(markup, highlight_regex, "search.match")

84	class LeftRail:
85	    """Prefix every line of a renderable with a thin colored left rail (``▎``).
86	
87	    The rail's vertical span marks a tool block's extent without a horizontal
88	    rule (which is already the message/conversation separator). Renders the
89	    child at reduced width so the rail fits inside its enclosing Panel.
90	    """
91	
92	    def __init__(self, renderable, style: str, glyph: str = "▎ ") -> None:
93	        self.renderable = renderable
94	        self.style = style
95	        self.glyph = glyph
96	
97	    def __rich_console__(
98	        self, console: Console, options: ConsoleOptions
99	    ) -> RenderResult:
100	        rail = Segment(self.glyph, console.get_style(self.style))
101	        inner = options.update_width(max(1, options.max_width - len(self.glyph)))
102	        lines = console.render_lines(self.renderable, inner, pad=False)
103	
104	        is_blank = lambda line: all(not segment.text.strip() for segment in line)
105	        start, end = 0, len(lines)
106	        while start < end and is_blank(lines[start]):
107	            start += 1
108	        while end > start and is_blank(lines[end - 1]):
109	            end -= 1
110	
111	        for line in lines[start:end]:
112	            yield rail
113	            yield from line
114	            yield Segment.line()

148	def _strip_read_line_numbers(text: str) -> tuple[str, int]:
149	    """Strip Read's ``<n>\\t`` line-number gutter, returning (code, first_line)."""
150	    lines = text.split("\n")
151	    stripped: list[str] = []
152	    first: int | None = None
153	    matched = 0
154	    for line in lines:
155	        match = re.match(r"\s*(\d+)\t(.*)$", line)
156	        if match:
157	            matched += 1
158	            first = first if first is not None else int(match.group(1))
159	            stripped.append(match.group(2))
160	        else:
161	            stripped.append(line)
162	    if matched < max(1, len(lines) // 2):
163	        return text, 1
164	    return "\n".join(stripped), first or 1

289	                    r"\\<\1\2\3>",
290	                    part.data,

# Test-Driven Development

## Philosophy

**Core principle**: Tests should verify behavior through public interfaces, not implementation details. Code can change entirely; tests shouldn't.

**Good tests** are integration-style: they exercise real code paths through public APIs. They describe _what_ the system does, not _how_ it does it. A good test reads like a specification - "user can checkout with valid cart" tells you exactly what capability exists. These tests survive refactors because they don't care about internal structure.

**Bad tests** are coupled to implementation. They mock internal collaborators, test private methods, or verify through external means (like querying a database directly instead of using the interface). The warning sign: your test breaks when you refactor, but behavior hasn't changed. If you rename an internal function and tests fail, those tests were testing implementation, not behavior.

See [tests.md](tests.md) for examples and [mocking.md](mocking.md) for mocking guidelines.

## Anti-Pattern: Horizontal Slices

**DO NOT write all tests first, then all implementation.** This is "horizontal slicing" - treating RED as "write all tests" and GREEN as "write all code."

This produces **crap tests**:

- Tests written in bulk test _imagined_ behavior, not _actual_ behavior
- You end up testing the _shape_ of things (data structures, function signatures) rather than user-facing behavior
- Tests become insensitive to real changes - they pass when behavior breaks, fail when behavior is fine
- You outrun your headlights, committing to test structure before understanding the implementation

**Correct approach**: Vertical slices via tracer bullets. One test → one implementation → repeat. Each test responds to what you learned from the previous cycle. Because you just wrote the code, you know exactly what behavior matters and how to verify it.

```
WRONG (horizontal):
  RED:   test1, test2, test3, test4, test5
  GREEN: impl1, impl2, impl3, impl4, impl5

RIGHT (vertical):
  RED→GREEN: test1→impl1
  RED→GREEN: test2→impl2
  RED→GREEN: test3→impl3
  ...
```

## Workflow

### 1. Planning

Before writing any code:

- [ ] Confirm with user what interface changes are needed
- [ ] Confirm with user which behaviors to test (prioritize)
- [ ] Identify opportunities for [deep modules](deep-modules.md) (small interface, deep implementation)
- [ ] Design interfaces for [testability](interface-design.md)
- [ ] List the behaviors to test (not implementation steps)
- [ ] Get user approval on the plan

Ask: "What should the public interface look like? Which behaviors are most important to test?"

**You can't test everything.** Confirm with the user exactly which behaviors matter most. Focus testing effort on critical paths and complex logic, not every possible edge case.

### 2. Tracer Bullet

Write ONE test that confirms ONE thing about the system:

```
RED:   Write test for first behavior → test fails
GREEN: Write minimal code to pass → test passes
```

This is your tracer bullet - proves the path works end-to-end.

### 3. Incremental Loop

For each remaining behavior:

```
RED:   Write next test → fails
GREEN: Minimal code to pass → passes
```

Rules:

- One test at a time
- Only enough code to pass current test
- Don't anticipate future tests
- Keep tests focused on observable behavior

### 4. Refactor

After all tests pass, look for [refactor candidates](refactoring.md):

- [ ] Extract duplication
- [ ] Deepen modules (move complexity behind simple interfaces)
- [ ] Apply SOLID principles where natural
- [ ] Consider what new code reveals about existing code
- [ ] Run tests after each refactor step

**Never refactor while RED.** Get to GREEN first.

## Checklist Per Cycle

```
[ ] Test describes behavior, not implementation
[ ] Test uses public interface only
[ ] Test would survive internal refactor
[ ] Code is minimal for this test
[ ] No speculative features added
```

<testing-tenets>
### Testing Tenets

<tests-must-be-meaningful priority="1">
When writing tests, make sure they're not "empty"—don't over-mock, and don't mock away the core of what you're testing.
False security is worse than having no tests at all.
Don't test implementation, test behavior.
The behavior under test should be based on—and faithfully reflect—the original spec or plan, not the implementation, to avoid circularity.
Fewer tests that are more focused, precise, and substantial are better than a larger number of meatless tests.
Insubstantial tests usually fall under the category of fooling one's self petitio principii–style—essentially, even if indirectly, by mocking aspects of the outcome you're supposed to be testing.
</tests-must-be-meaningful>

<tests-must-be-informative priority="2">
Make use of `assert`'s second positional argument to help the developer understand the error.
<negative-example description="uninformative assert expression">
`assert foo`
</negative-example>
<positive-example description="informative assert expression">
`assert foo, f"Expected 'foo' to be truthy. Got: {foo=!r}"`
</positive-example>
</tests-must-be-informative>

<tests-must-not-cause-exceptions-themselves priority="2">
Tests must be robust. Test that cause errors "on accident" overshadow the behavior under test.
<negative-example description="hard-coding a symbol path is brittle" example-id="1">
`with patch("module.function"): ...`
</negative-example>
<positive-example description="using the actual symbol is robust" example-id="1">
```
import module.function
with patch(module.function): ...
```
</positive-example>
<negative-example description="Raises a `KeyError` if the key isn't present, which is not the behavior under test. Fails for the wrong reason." example-id="2">
`assert my_dict["nested"]["key"] == "value", ...`
</negative-example>
<positive-example example-id="2">
`assert my_dict.get("nested", {}).get("key") == "value", ...`
</positive-example>
</tests-must-not-cause-exceptions-themselves>

</testing-tenets>

8	def truncate_middle(s: str, max_len: int = 500) -> str:
9	    """Shorten a string by replacing its middle with an ellipsis block."""
10	    placeholder = "\n...\n"
11	    if max_len < len(placeholder):
12	        placeholder = "..."[:max_len]
13	
14	    if len(s) <= max_len - len(placeholder):
15	        return s
16	
17	    if max_len <= len(placeholder):
18	        return placeholder[:max_len]
19	
20	    remaining = max_len - len(placeholder)
21	    first_half = remaining // 2 + (remaining % 2)
22	    second_half = remaining // 2
23	
24	    return s[:first_half] + placeholder + s[-second_half:]

81	_AGE_UNITS: tuple[tuple[float, str], ...] = (
82	    (60.0, "now"),
83	    (3600.0, "m"),
84	    (86400.0, "h"),
85	    (7 * 86400.0, "d"),
86	    (30 * 86400.0, "w"),
87	    (365 * 86400.0, "mo"),
88	)
89	
90	
91	def humanize_age(then: datetime, now: datetime | None = None) -> str:
92	    """Render the age of ``then`` as a compact token like ``24m`` or ``2w``.
93	
94	    >>> base = datetime(2026, 6, 15, 12, 0, 0)
95	    >>> humanize_age(datetime(2026, 6, 15, 11, 59, 30), base)
96	    'now'
97	    >>> humanize_age(datetime(2026, 6, 15, 11, 36, 0), base)
98	    '24m'
99	    >>> humanize_age(datetime(2026, 6, 15, 9, 0, 0), base)
100	    '3h'
101	    >>> humanize_age(datetime(2026, 6, 14, 12, 0, 0), base)
102	    '1d'
103	    >>> humanize_age(datetime(2026, 6, 1, 12, 0, 0), base)
104	    '2w'
105	    >>> humanize_age(datetime(2026, 1, 15, 12, 0, 0), base)
106	    '5mo'
107	    >>> humanize_age(datetime(2024, 6, 15, 12, 0, 0), base)
108	    '2y'
109	    """
110	    seconds = ((now or datetime.now()) - then).total_seconds()
111	    if seconds < 60:
112	        return "now"
113	    divisors = (1, 60, 3600, 86400, 7 * 86400, 30 * 86400)
114	    for (ceiling, unit), divisor in zip(_AGE_UNITS, divisors):
115	        if seconds < ceiling:
116	            return f"{int(seconds // divisor)}{unit}"
117	    return f"{int(seconds // (365 * 86400))}y"
118	
119	
120	def age_style(then: datetime, now: datetime | None = None) -> str:
121	    """Return the theme style token for an age, brightest for the most recent.
122	
123	    >>> base = datetime(2026, 6, 15, 12, 0, 0)
124	    >>> age_style(datetime(2026, 6, 15, 9, 0, 0), base)
125	    'search.age.now'
126	    >>> age_style(datetime(2026, 6, 12, 12, 0, 0), base)
127	    'search.age.week'
128	    >>> age_style(datetime(2026, 5, 20, 12, 0, 0), base)
129	    'search.age.month'
130	    >>> age_style(datetime(2025, 6, 15, 12, 0, 0), base)
131	    'search.age.old'
132	    """
133	    seconds = ((now or datetime.now()) - then).total_seconds()
134	    if seconds < 86400:
135	        return "search.age.now"
136	    if seconds < 7 * 86400:
137	        return "search.age.week"
138	    if seconds < 30 * 86400:
139	        return "search.age.month"
140	    return "search.age.old"
141	
142	
143	def elide_to_width(text: str, width: int, *, where: str = "tail") -> str:
144	    """Shorten ``text`` to ``width`` columns on a single line with an ellipsis.
145	
146	    >>> elide_to_width("hello world", 20)
147	    'hello world'
148	    >>> elide_to_width("hello world", 8)
149	    'hello w…'
150	    >>> elide_to_width("/a/very/long/path/here", 12, where="middle")
151	    '/a/ver…/here'
152	    """
153	    if len(text) <= width:
154	        return text
155	    if width <= 1:
156	        return "…"[:width]
157	    available = width - 1
158	    if where == "middle":
159	        left = (available + 1) // 2
160	        right = available // 2
161	        return text[:left] + "…" + (text[-right:] if right else "")
162	    return text[:available] + "…"
163

1	#!/usr/bin/env zsh -i

4	echo "Running structured rendering tests..."
5	DATA_FILE_SYNTHETIC="tests/data/synthetic_flags.jsonl"
6	GOLDEN_FILE="tests/data/golden_xml_output.txt"
7	
8	# Helper: strip ANSI codes
9	strip_ansi() {

13	# Test 1: XML output unchanged (regression prevention)
14	echo "Testing XML output unchanged (golden reference)..."
15	actual=$($CC_CMD -T -t "$DATA_FILE_SYNTHETIC" --color=never 2>/dev/null)
16	expected=$(cat "$GOLDEN_FILE")
17	if [[ "$actual" != "$expected" ]]; then
18	    echo "❌ XML output differs from golden reference"
19	    echo "=== EXPECTED ==="
20	    echo "$expected" | head -20
21	    echo "=== ACTUAL ==="
22	    echo "$actual" | head -20
23	    exit 1
24	fi
25	echo "  ✓ XML output matches golden reference"
26	
27	# Test 2: Rich thinking renders tag-free under a ✻ marker (not <thinking> tags).
28	# tests/test_colored_rendering.py pins the colored structure in detail; this is the
29	# CLI-seam check that the same tag-free shape reaches the terminal through `ch`.
30	echo "Testing Rich thinking renders tag-free..."
31	output=$($CC_CMD -T "$DATA_FILE_SYNTHETIC" --color=always 2>&1 | strip_ansi)
32	assert_contains "$output" "✻ thinking"
33	assert_contains "$output" "I should reply hello"
34	assert_not_contains "$output" "<thinking>"
35	echo "  ✓ Rich thinking is tag-free (✻ marker)"

37	# Test 3: Rich tools render tag-free as ⏺ call / ⎿ result headers (not <tool-*> tags).
38	echo "Testing Rich tools render tag-free..."
39	output=$($CC_CMD -t "$DATA_FILE_SYNTHETIC" --color=always 2>&1 | strip_ansi)
40	assert_contains "$output" "⏺"
41	assert_contains "$output" "⎿"
42	assert_contains "$output" "result"
43	assert_not_contains "$output" "<tool-input"
44	assert_not_contains "$output" "<tool-output"
45	echo "  ✓ Rich tools are tag-free (⏺/⎿ markers)"
46	
47	# Test 4: colored and plain views diverge by design — colored is tag-free, while
48	# plain (--color=never) keeps the XML tags (the form meant for piping to tools/LLMs).
49	echo "Testing colored is tag-free while plain keeps tags..."

51	rich=$($CC_CMD -T -t "$DATA_FILE_SYNTHETIC" --color=always 2>&1 | strip_ansi)
52	assert_contains "$plain" "<thinking>"
53	assert_contains "$plain" "<tool-input"
54	assert_not_contains "$rich" "<thinking>"
55	assert_not_contains "$rich" "<tool-input"

62	assert_contains "$output" "Assistant"
63	assert_not_contains "$output" "## User"

1	"""Characterization tests for the colored Rich rendering of parse and search.
2	
3	These pin *observable output* through the public commands (`cmd_parse`,
4	`cmd_search`), never the internal renderers. A refactor is free to rename or
5	merge the panel/rail/tool helpers as long as what reaches the terminal is
6	preserved — these tests guard that, plus the colored-vs-plain split the redesign
7	depends on. The rest of the suite exercises the plain/data path but not the
8	colored render structure, which is what these cover.
9	"""
10	
11	from __future__ import annotations

38	               model: str = "claude-opus-4-8", ts: str = "2026-06-16T11:00:00Z") -> dict:
39	    body = content if content is not None else [{"type": "text", "text": text}]
40	    return {"type": "assistant", "timestamp": ts, "cwd": "/tmp/proj",
41	            "message": {"role": "assistant", "model": model, "content": body}}

45	    return {"type": "user", "timestamp": ts, "cwd": "/tmp/proj",

49	def _render_colored(monkeypatch, func, *args, styles: bool = False,
50	                    width: int = 96, **kwargs) -> str:
51	    """Run a command against a recording truecolor console and return its output."""
52	    recorder = Console(theme=APP_THEME, width=width, force_terminal=True,
53	                       color_system="truecolor", record=True)
54	    monkeypatch.setattr(console_mod, "_console", recorder)

146	def test_colored_parse_title_without_custom_title_leads_with_id(tmp_path, monkeypatch):

I've fully traced the seam, and I found something that changes the premise. Let me lay it out and get your call on direction, because the right move forks on a value judgment.

**The binding constraint isn't the golden test — it's `test_short_modifier.py`.** The golden reference (`test_structured_rendering.sh` Test 1) is generated *without* `--short`, so a change to wrapping order wouldn't trip it. What actually pins the bytes is `test_short_modifier.py`, which asserts the XML tool body is **exactly 500 characters including the ` ```sh ` fence scaffolding** (across Claude/Codex/Pi). Today's flow shortens the already-wrapped `content` string, so the fence is counted inside the 500-char budget. If you instead shorten the raw payload once and re-wrap, the body becomes ~510 and that invariant breaks.

**Why this blocks the literal "shorten once."** The three representations don't just duplicate data — they encode three *different* shortening semantics: XML counts scaffolding toward the budget; the colored path shortens `input_data`/`output_text` as raw fields (Edit's old/new shortened independently for the diff); JSON shortens the raw dict. There's no single shorten call that simultaneously yields XML's "500 incl. fence" body *and* colored's separately-shortened `old_string`/`new_string`. Dropping the denormalized `content` doesn't remove that complexity — it just relocates the scaffolding-inclusive shorten into the XML renderer.

**The interesting part:** that "500 including the fence" rule is arguably an implementation artifact, not a real spec. Budgeting the *payload* to 500 and then adding the fence is, if anything, more correct. So whether to preserve it is genuinely your call, not something I should silently break.

The consumers are exactly three (`render_tool_xml`, `render_tool_rich`, and the one shorten block in `model.py`) — no hidden coupling — so any of these is mechanically safe.

questions.question: Given that a single shorten call can't both keep the XML body at exactly 500 chars-including-fence AND feed the colored path's independently-shortened Edit diff, how do you want to resolve the unification?

options.label: Encapsulate, keep output (Recommended)
options.description: Keep the three representations but move the three-way shorten into one cohesive operation on ToolParts (e.g. ToolParts.shorten(width)), co-located with the type. Each renderer still formats on its own terms; every current byte (XML/raw/colored/JSON) is preserved; the 'forgot to shorten one copy' bug-class is structurally closed. Smallest safe diff, but it doesn't literally 'shorten once' — it makes the all-three-together invariant impossible to forget.

options.label: Normalize, relax 500-incl-fence
options.description: Drop the denormalized `content` field; ToolParts carries one raw structured payload that each renderer derives its view from; shorten the payload literally once. Truly achieves 'shorten once' and is arguably more correct (the 500 budget covers the payload, not payload+fence). Cost: XML --short bytes shift, so test_short_modifier.py's exact-500 assertions get updated to expect payload-500. Intentionally changes observable --short output.

options.label: Skip — already fixed
options.description: The recent commit (56d47c2) already closed the real leak, and the three-way shorten now lives in a single block in model.py. The remaining bug-class (someone adds a 4th representation and forgets it) is speculative. Per YAGNI, leave it as is.

Truly achieves 'shorten once' and is arguably more correct (the 500 budget covers the payload, not payload+fence). Cost: XML --short bytes shift, so test_short_modifier.py's exact-500 assertions get updated to expect payload-500. Intentionally changes observable --short output, BUT i have a hunch that we are over focused on shortening tools specifically, when --short shortens everything. i think option (2) is the best way to tackle shortening tools. but does it also cleanly apply to "shortening whatever"? i have a feeling that either the answer is YES or "with a tiny modification, YES". one shortening mechanism to rule them all". You can now continue with these answers in mind.

def _iter_visible_tools(
        self,
        flags: ConversationFlags,
        id_map: dict[str, str],
    ) -> Iterator[dict]:
        """Yield each visible tool dict, shortened at the source when asked.

        Shortening once here — on the raw tool dict via shorten_data — is the single
        shortening point for tools, mirroring how text, thinking and plans are
        shortened at the source. tool_to_parts/tool_to_json then build their views
        (XML content, the colored diff/highlight, JSON) from already-short data, so
        no representation can be left untruncated.
        """
        for tool in self.tools:
            show, filter_short = self._should_show_tool(tool, flags.show_tools, id_map)
            if not show:
                continue
            if flags.shorten or filter_short:
                tool = shorten_data(tool, width=flags.shorten_width)
            yield tool

    def _append_tool_parts(
        self,
        parts: list[MessagePart],
        flags: ConversationFlags,
        tool_id_map: dict[str, str] | None,
    ) -> None:
        """Append visible tool parts based on filters."""
        id_map = self._tool_name_id_map(flags.show_tools, tool_id_map)
        for tool in self._iter_visible_tools(flags, id_map):
            parts.append(MessagePart(MessagePartKind.TOOL, tool_to_parts(tool, id_map)))

    def _visible_tool_json_content(
        self,
        flags: ConversationFlags,
        tool_id_map: dict[str, str] | None,
    ) -> list[dict[str, object]]:
        """Return visible tools in structured JSON form."""
        id_map = self._tool_name_id_map(flags.show_tools, tool_id_map)
        return [tool_to_json(tool, id_map) for tool in self._iter_visible_tools(flags, id_map)]

name: gotchas
description: A gotcha is fairly confidently signing off on something that later on proved to be at least partially wrong due to wrong assumptions.
---

# GOTCHAS

## 2026-05-04

Assumed sidechain discovery layout didn't have to match fork output layout: in our case, reading Claude agents from `subagents/` while still writing forks to the project root.

Assumed a selection must fully materialize every candidate before filtering. When a query needs only a few fields and can short-circuit, eager full materialization is the trap: probe the minimal facets the predicate needs, push the filter to the scan, and stop at the first match. In our case, `ch -1 -d ...` loaded full metadata and reread files for `cwd` instead of streaming `cwd` newest-first and stopping.

Assumed an input was already ordered the way a short-circuit depended on. Optimizing a scan to stop early silently makes correctness depend on iteration order — a dependency the eager version never had. In our case, the dir fast path did `reversed(files)` assuming stat-mtime order, but the list was discovery-ordered, so it matched the wrong session.

1	# Changelog
2	
3	All notable changes to the `conversations` skill.
4	
5	---
6	## [2026-06-28] Message role colors get a coherent palette
7	
8	### Changed
9	
10	- The per-message role hues are now drawn from one named palette in `theme.py` (borrowed from the One Atom Dark theme) instead of eight ad-hoc hexes that crowded the blue–purple range. Each role group gets a well-separated hue: user blue, assistant magenta, agent cyan, recap green, compaction amber, session-rename red. The three `user-*` tags still share blue, since they are one actor.
11	- Role badge chips switched from white to dark ink text so they stay legible on the lighter pastel backgrounds.
12	- The message-body styles (`tool.call`, `tool.error`, `diff.add`, `diff.remove`) now reference the same palette, folding two near-identical reds (`#e06c75` and `#e27881`) into one.
13	
14	---
15	## [2026-06-27] Negative recent indices use transcript recency
16	
17	### Changed
18	
19	- Recent negative selectors (`ch -1`, `ch -2`, and filtered variants such as `ch -d DIR -1`) now order candidates by the last timestamp inside each JSONL transcript instead of filesystem mtime. Files without a readable in-band timestamp keep the existing filesystem-mtime fallback, and provider/dir/date filters still use the cheap probe path rather than full metadata loading.
20	
21	---
22	## [2026-06-24] Worst-case performance fast paths
23	
24	### Changed
25	
26	- `ch` now avoids global session resolution for explicit JSONL/raw stdin or pasted content, while preserving one-line piped session-id resolution. `ch <session> -ll` resolves and prints the display id without reading/parsing the session body.
27	- Canonical UUID misses now stop after exact-id lookup instead of scanning title/summary facets across the pool. Title/summary fallback resolution now JSON-parses only raw lines that can carry summaries or current-title records.
28	- Plain ASCII literal searches use a chunked byte candidate gate before full text reads; non-ASCII, regex-shaped, and render-dependent searches still fall back. Survivors always pass the existing semantic confirmation path, so raw-byte hits do not bypass visibility rules.
29	- `ch search . -ll` has a narrow projection fast path for default visibility only. It streams ids without metadata loading or `SessionScan` on eligible files, falls back for branchable/uncertain files, and mirrors hidden protocol/tool/thinking/task-notification behavior. On the local ~2.3k-file pool this reduced `search . -ll` from ~7.5–8s to ~3.5s; literal no-hit search is ~1.35s, UUID miss ~0.63s, and 35MB stdin parse ~0.48s.
30	
31	---
32	## [2026-06-22] `ch info --format json`
33	
34	### Added
35	
36	- `ch info <session> -f json` (alongside the default `-f text`) prints the same statistics as a flat, snake-cased JSON document for piping into `jq`. Root keys: `name`, `file`, `id`, `total_duration_api`, `total_duration_wall` (humanized strings, or `null` when absent), `model`, `usage_by_model` (per model → a CostStats), `messages` (`user`, `assistant`, `tool_calls`, `tool_results`, `total`), and `tokens` (a CostStats). A CostStats is `{input, output, cache_read, cache_write, total, cost}`, so the session total cost is `tokens.cost` and each model's cost is its own entry's `cost`.
37	- A `model` field reports the dominant model by total token usage. The text report adds a humanized `Model:` line between the wall duration and the usage breakdown (`claude-opus-4-8` → `Claude Opus 4.8`), dropping any provider prefix and date/`@` stamp.
38	- The aggregated `SessionInfo` is the single typed source of truth: the text report reads it directly, and `session_info_as_dict` is the lone serialization boundary that projects it to JSON primitives. JSON durations are numeric seconds (the lower-level form the report humanizes), rather than pre-humanized strings.
39	
40	### Changed
41	
42	- The text report's cost moved into the `Tokens` block as a single `Cost: <total>` line (under `Total:`), replacing the standalone `Cost` section with its redundant `Total:` sub-line. In JSON the total cost is `tokens.cost`; there is no separate root `cost` key.
43	
44	---
45	## [2026-06-21] Add `info` command for per-session statistics (Claude and PI)
46	
47	### Added
48	
49	- `ch info <session>` aggregates and prints one session's statistics: name, file, id, wall-clock and API durations, per-model token usage with cost, message counts (user, assistant, tool calls, tool results), aggregate token totals, and total cost. It resolves a session the same way parse does (id, name, recent negative index, or file path) and is currently scoped to Claude and PI; a Codex or Antigravity session is rejected with a clear error rather than producing a half-filled report. Logic lives in `chats.commands.info`.
50	- Wall-clock duration is the span between the first and last in-band timestamps. API duration is shown only when real generation-time data exists — for Claude that is the sum of `system`/`turn_duration` `durationMs` entries (emitted only by recent CLI versions); PI records none, so the line is omitted rather than inferred from timestamp gaps.
51	- Token usage is grouped by the per-message model, so a session that switched models mid-stream reports each model separately. Claude writes one API response across several JSONL lines that repeat the same `message.id` and `usage`, so usage and the assistant-message count are deduplicated by `message.id`; `<synthetic>` placeholder and API-error lines are excluded. Tool calls are counted by distinct `tool_use` block id and tool results by distinct `tool_result` `tool_use_id`, so the split-line layout never double-counts.
52	- Where the file states a value, `info` reads it rather than recomputing: PI's per-message `totalTokens` is summed for the token total (Claude has no such field, so there it is the sum of the four categories), and cost comes straight from PI's stored `usage.cost.total`. Claude stores no cost, so it is computed from a per-model price table (cache reads at 0.1x input) that tolerates bare and date-stamped model ids. Cache writes are priced per TTL bucket from the `cache_creation` breakdown Claude records — `ephemeral_1h_input_tokens` at 2x input and `ephemeral_5m_input_tokens` at 1.25x — which matches Claude Code's 1-hour-cache billing; absent the breakdown the aggregate write count falls back to the 5-minute rate.
53	- The aggregate token total and the message total both include every category — cache-write tokens are part of the token total, and tool results count toward the message total while tool calls (which live inside assistant messages) are reported separately.
54	
55	---
56	## [2026-06-21] Capture user-initiated `/fork` subagents under `--agents`
57	
58	### Added
59	
60	- `-a, --agents` now also splices user-initiated `/fork` transcripts into the timeline, not just agent-initiated `Task` subagents. A `/fork` is a detached sidechain: the main session keeps only the `/fork` command and the returning `<task-notification>`, while the fork's transcript lives in `subagents/agent-{slug}-{taskId}.jsonl` whose leading `fork-context-ref` links back to the parent via `parentSessionId` (no in-thread `Task` anchor). Discovery previously matched a subagent file by its first line's `sessionId`, which a fork's `fork-context-ref` header lacks, so every fork was silently dropped; `chats.commands.resolve.find_agent_files_for_session` now also matches `fork-context-ref.parentSessionId`.
61	- A fork is labelled `Fork` (its `## Fork` header and colored badge) to set it apart from agent-initiated `Task` subagents, which stay `Agent`. The distinction is also machine-readable: a fork carries `subagent_type="fork"` (read from its `.meta.json` `agentType`), already surfaced as an XML/JSON attribute on the `<agent>` block.
62	
63	---
64	## [2026-06-21] Detect and gate off-main-branch (rewound) Claude messages
65	
66	### Added
67	
68	- A Claude transcript is a tree, not a line: rewinding to an earlier point and re-prompting forks it, leaving the abandoned attempt interleaved in file order as if it were linear history. `ch` now detects these abandoned branches and omits them by default, so a printed conversation follows only the main thread. The new `-b, --branches` flag includes them, each tagged with a `branch="N"` attribute (`-f json`: a `branch` key) and a `⑂N` chip in colored output. It is its own flag, deliberately independent of `-t, --tools`.
69	- The branch id groups a detour by its *head* — the first message that left the main line — so all messages from one rewind share an id while separate rewinds from the same fork point stay distinct.
70	- The main thread is resolved per era. Real eras are the session start and each `/compact` boundary (a boundary is a fresh `parentUuid: null` root, making a compacted file a forest); a rewind to the *first* message — a second null-parent user root — is an abandoned detour, recognized across compaction via the boundary's `logicalParentUuid`. Within an era the active branch is picked by the latest `last-prompt` `leafUuid` and then followed *down* to its tip and up to the root (longest continuation when no leaf is recorded), so the reply below the recorded leaf stays on the main thread; the leaf is preferred over subtree depth because the active branch can be shorter than an abandoned one. Compaction seams are never treated as branches, and resolution is iterative to stay safe on very deep threads. Claude only; the logic lives in `chats.parsing._resolve_branch_map`.
71	
72	### Fixed
73	
74	- A transcript snippet whose head is truncated has no `parentUuid: null` root; the resolver now treats a parent absent from the file as an era root, so partial logs are not wholly mislabeled as off-branch.
75	
76	---
77	## [2026-06-21] Render Claude compaction summaries as Compaction blocks
78	
79	### Added
80	
81	- Claude `type: "user"` entries flagged `isCompactSummary: true` (the summary injected when a conversation is continued past its context limit) now render as a `<compaction>` block with a `## Compaction` header, shown by default like `<recap>` rather than as a regular `<user-message>`. In colored output the block gets its own fuchsia hue (`#a21caf`) and a "Compaction" badge; `-f json` emits `type: "compaction"`.
82	
83	---
84	## [2026-06-18] Redesign the colored view as tag-free panels
85	
86	### Changed
87	
88	- Colored output (`--color=auto`/`always`) no longer wraps messages in XML tags. Parse renders each message as its own rounded panel titled with a colored role badge (role hue, index, model); `ch search` renders each matching conversation as one panel whose border hue cycles per conversation. The XML tags remain only in plain output (`--color=never`, `-f raw`) — the form meant for piping to tools or LLMs (`-f json` is structured separately and unaffected).
89	- Inside a message, thinking renders under a `✻ thinking` marker, subagent tasks under `✻ subagent task`, and tools as tag-free `⏺` call / `⎿` result headers over a colored left rail. Edit calls render as a unified diff and a Read result is syntax-highlighted by file extension; other tools fall back to fenced markdown.
90	- Internal cleanup: removed the dead `render_messages_with_rich` path and unified the duplicate header builders into one badge, dropped the unused `ContentBlockInfo.rich_style` field, deduped the search match-count behind one helper and `SearchHit.match_count`, and stored role hues bare so the panel border no longer re-parses a composite style string.
91	
92	### Fixed
93	
94	- Colored output silently dropped message text containing attributed XML-like tags (e.g. `<div class="box">`): Rich's Markdown treated them as unknown HTML and stripped them. Such tags are now escaped before rendering so they survive literally (bare tags like `<thinking>` were already handled, attributed ones were not).
95	
96	---
97	## [2026-06-16] Stream search results to the terminal as they are found
98	
99	### Changed
100	
101	- `ch search` now displays each matching session the moment it is confirmed instead of scanning the whole pool, sorting, then paging. On a ~1900-file pool, the first result appears in well under a second (e.g. ~0.76s) rather than after the full ~9–13s scan, making a bare `ch search <pattern>` usable again.
102	- Paged, colored output streams through `less -r` via a new `StreamingPager`: `less` is spawned up front and each hit's Rich-rendered ANSI is written and flushed as it is produced (instead of Rich's `Console.pager()`, which buffers everything until the scan finishes). Quitting `less` early stops the search and tears down cleanly, mirroring `UnicodeSafePager`'s SIGPIPE handling.
103	- Display order is now scan order — newest first by filesystem mtime — rather than a post-scan re-sort by in-band (semantic) modified time. This matches the precedent already set by recent-index resolution and is what enables streaming; the two orderings are near-identical in practice (they differ only for artifacts like forks whose file mtime and last in-band timestamp diverge).
104	- The colored `ch search -l` list view streams its rows; its `N sessions · newest first` line now prints as a trailing summary (the count is only known once scanning finishes), and per-row provider labels are decided from whether the searched candidate pool spans multiple providers rather than from the providers among the final hits.
105	- `ch search -r/--raw` stays buffered: its single-visible-message special case needs every hit up front.
106	
107	---
108	## [2026-06-12] Classify Claude background-task notifications as the TaskNotification tool
109	
110	### Changed
111	
112	- Claude `type: "user"` entries carrying a `<task-notification>...</task-notification>` payload (emitted when a background `Agent` task finishes) no longer render as regular user messages. They now parse into a synthetic `tool_use` named `TaskNotification`: hidden by default, shown with `-t`, and filterable by name like any tool (`-t TaskNotification`, `-t !TaskNotification`).
113	- Three fields become `<tool-input>` XML attributes — the shortened `tool_use_id` (which links back to the originating `Agent` dispatch), `status`, and `summary` — and the `result` markdown becomes the tool body. Double quotes embedded in attribute values are downgraded to single quotes rather than escaped. JSON output exposes the same fields on a typed `tool-input` block.
114	
115	---
116	## [2026-06-11] Prefix auto-generated rename titles with session date and cwd
117	
118	### Changed
119	
120	- `ch rename --auto` titles are now assembled programmatically as `MM-DD <cwd name> <generated phrase>` (date from the first message's in-band timestamp, falling back to file birth time), e.g. `06-11 chats fix flaky tests`. The LLM prompt only generates the phrase and is oblivious to both date and cwd. Explicit renames are unaffected; `--dry-run` prints the full title.
121	
122	---
123	## [2026-06-10] Add boolean `and`/`or` search operators
124	
125	### Added
126	
127	- `ch search` patterns now support lowercase `and`/`or` operators with parentheses, e.g. `'docker and timeout'`, `'deploy and (staging or prod)'`. `and` binds tighter than `or`.
128	- Terms are evaluated session-wide: `and` terms may match in different messages, summaries, or the current title. Displayed matches are the union of messages matching any term.

Tools now match how `text`, `thinking`, and `plan` were already shortened — the payload to width, wrappers outside it — so there is a single shortening rule across the whole renderer. `test_short_modifier.py` and `test_tool_filter.py` were updated to assert the payload length inside the fence; the unshortened golden XML reference is unchanged.

Done. All tests pass, the change is in, and the CHANGELOG records the decision.

## What I did

I implemented your chosen direction (normalize, relax the 500-including-fence rule), and your hunch turned out to make the change *smaller* than the option as written — I did **not** need to drop the `content` field at all.

The whole fix is in `Message._iter_visible_tools` (a new shared generator in `model.py`): it shortens each visible tool's **raw dict once** with `shorten_data`, and then `tool_to_parts` / `tool_to_json` build every view (the XML fence, the colored Edit-diff and Read-highlight, the JSON) from already-short data. The old three-way shorten block — which truncated the pre-wrapped `content` string separately from the raw `input_data` and `output_text`, and was the exact source of the recent leak regression — is gone. Both tool paths (`_append_tool_parts` and `_visible_tool_json_content`) now route through that one loop, so `_visible_tool_json_content` collapsed to a one-line comprehension. Net negative lines, one shortening point, no representation that can drift.

Dropping `content` only looked necessary under byte-preservation; once you relaxed that, shortening the source dict makes `content` shortened-by-construction, so the denormalized field is harmless again.

## Your "one mechanism to rule them all" question

**Yes — cleanly, no modification needed.** `shorten_data(data, width)` already *is* that mechanism: it recurses dicts/lists and truncates every string leaf to `width` (calling `truncate_middle`, which is just its leaf primitive). It was already shortening message text, plans, and the JSON tool dict. The tool *parts* path was the lone holdout, only because the pre-wrapped `content` forced a separate truncate whose budget swallowed the fence.

The deeper thing your instinct caught: `text`, `thinking`, and `plan` were *already* doing the correct thing — budget the payload to `width`, leave the wrapper (the `<thinking>` tags, the panel) outside it. Tools were the one place where scaffolding counted against the budget, which is why a 500-width Bash body really only showed ~490 chars of command. After this change, tools join the rest, and the whole renderer now obeys a single rule: **shorten the raw payload at the source; wrappers and fences always sit outside the budget.** So the observable shift is a 500-width tool body becoming `` ``` `` + 500 + `` ``` `` instead of 500 total — which is the more correct reading of "shorten to 500."

I left `thinking` calling `truncate_middle` directly rather than `shorten_data`; for a known single string they're identical, so it's the same mechanism's leaf primitive applied without the dispatch. Not worth a change.

## Verification

I followed the red→green loop: flipped the pinned assertions in `test_short_modifier.py` to the payload-budgeted semantics first (watched the three tool-body tests fail at inner=490), then implemented to green. A second wave — `test_tool_filter.py`'s three `TestPerToolShortening` tests — pinned the same old fence-inclusive length and needed the identical update. Full suite green (554 passed), including the unshortened golden XML reference, which is byte-identical. The pyright notes that surfaced are all pre-existing (the `str | ToolParts` union access in the tests and the `show_all` return type) — none from this change, and per your rule I left them alone.

content:
Committed as `0f452bf`. Now your two questions — I traced both through `truncate_middle`/`shorten_data` and every call site.

## 1. No, there's no aggregate cap — the budget is strictly per string leaf

`shorten_data` recurses a structure and caps **each individual string** at the budget; it keeps no running total. So:

- **A single wide object** with N string values can reach roughly N × width. The everyday case is `Edit`, which renders `old_string` + `new_string` and so lands at ~2× width even at the default 500. A generic/unknown tool that falls back to a JSON dump with many string keys multiplies further — every leaf is independently truncated to 500, nothing bounds their sum.
- **A whole message** is even less bounded: `text` (≤width) + `thinking` (≤width) + `plan` (≤width) + each visible tool (k×width), with no ceiling on the total. The same is true in `forking.py`, which uses the same two primitives the same per-leaf way.

Nowhere in the codebase is there a total-body budget. In practice this rarely bites because real tool inputs have a handful of keys, but you're right that the guarantee is "each value is bounded," not "the rendered object is bounded." Adding a true cap would be a design decision (which leaf to sacrifice, or truncate the rendered whole?), so I'd leave it unless you've actually seen a body blow up — the per-leaf cap already prevents the pathological single-giant-string case, which is the common one.

## 2. "width" is a misnomer — it's a total character count, and your worry is unfounded

Your hunch was that short-lined text might escape shortening, but it doesn't. `truncate_middle` checks `len(s) <= max_len`, and `len(s)` is the **total character count of the whole string, newlines included** — not a per-line column width. A 10,000-line file of 5-char lines is ~60,000 characters, far over 500, so it's middle-truncated like anything else. The only thing that escapes is a string whose *total* length is under the budget, regardless of shape.

So the name is the real issue, not the behavior: `shorten_width` / the `width=` keyword actually means "max total characters" (the underlying `truncate_middle` parameter is honestly named `max_len`). There *is* a genuinely column-based helper — `elide_to_width` — but that's separate single-line display elision (used for the tool-header key argument), not part of the `shorten_data` path. Renaming `width` → `max_chars` would be clearer but touches many call sites (`utils.py`, `model.py`, `cli.py`, `forking.py`), so it's pure churn I wouldn't do unless you want it.

Goal was unifying tool shortening so it happens once. That's done, committed as 0f452bf, and I answered your follow-ups about per-leaf budgeting and the misnamed "width." Nothing pending; awaiting your next direction.

Good catch to insist on it — `total_size` would actually re-introduce the Q1 confusion (it implies an aggregate cap, which doesn't exist; the limit is per-string-leaf). Let me scope the rename precisely so I don't touch the *legitimate* display widths (console/panel width), then do it.

92	def _replace_stem_suffix(
93	    source_path: Path,
94	    source_session_id: str,
95	    new_session_id: str,
96	    separator: str,
97	) -> Path:
98	    stem = source_path.stem
99	    if source_session_id and stem.endswith(source_session_id):
100	        new_stem = stem[: -len(source_session_id)] + new_session_id
101	    else:
102	        prefix, sep, _suffix = stem.rpartition(separator)
103	        new_stem = (
104	            f"{prefix}{sep}{new_session_id}" if prefix and sep else new_session_id
105	        )
106	    return source_path.with_name(f"{new_stem}{source_path.suffix}")

191	def _filter_claude_assistant_content(
192	    content: object,
193	    flags: ConversationFlags,
194	    id_map: dict[str, str],
195	    *,
196	    show_message_text: bool,
197	) -> list[dict]:
198	    if not isinstance(content, list):
199	        return []
200	
201	    kept_items: list[dict] = []
202	    for item in content:
203	        if not isinstance(item, dict):
204	            continue
205	
206	        item_type = item.get("type")
207	        if item_type == "text":
208	            if show_message_text and item.get("text", "").strip():
209	                kept_items.append(copy.deepcopy(item))
210	            continue
211	
212	        if item_type == "thinking":
213	            if not (show_message_text and flags.show_thinking):
214	                continue
215	            kept_item = copy.deepcopy(item)
216	            if flags.shorten or flags.shorten_thinking:
217	                kept_item["thinking"] = truncate_middle(
218	                    kept_item.get("thinking", ""),
219	                    max_len=flags.shorten_width,
220	                )
221	            kept_items.append(kept_item)
222	            continue
223	
224	        if item_type != "tool_use":
225	            continue
226	
227	        if item.get("name") == "ExitPlanMode":
228	            if show_message_text and flags.show_plans:
229	                kept_items.append(copy.deepcopy(item))
230	            continue
231	
232	        if item.get("name") == "Task" and flags.show_agents:
233	            kept_items.append(copy.deepcopy(item))
234	            continue
235	
236	        tool_payload = {
237	            "type": "tool_use",
238	            "id": item.get("id"),
239	            "name": item.get("name"),
240	            "input": item.get("input", {}),
241	        }
242	        show_tool, should_shorten = resolve_tool_visibility(
243	            tool_payload, flags.show_tools, id_map
244	        )
245	        if not show_tool:
246	            continue
247	
248	        kept_tool = _shorten_tool_payload(
249	            tool_payload,
250	            should_shorten,
251	            width=flags.shorten_width,
252	        )
253	        kept_items.append({
254	            **copy.deepcopy(item),
255	            "input": kept_tool.get("input", {}),
256	        })
257	
258	    return kept_items

261	def _filter_claude_user_content(
262	    content: object,
263	    flags: ConversationFlags,
264	    id_map: dict[str, str],
265	) -> tuple[list[object], list[tuple[dict, bool]]]:
266	    if isinstance(content, str):
267	        return ([content] if flags.show_user_messages and content else []), []
268	
269	    if not isinstance(content, list):
270	        return [], []
271	
272	    kept_items: list[object] = []
273	    kept_tool_results: list[tuple[dict, bool]] = []
274	    for item in content:
275	        if not isinstance(item, dict):
276	            if flags.show_user_messages:
277	                kept_items.append(copy.deepcopy(item))
278	            continue
279	
280	        if item.get("type") != "tool_result":
281	            if flags.show_user_messages:
282	                kept_items.append(copy.deepcopy(item))
283	            continue
284	
285	        tool_payload = {
286	            "type": "tool_result",
287	            "tool_use_id": item.get("tool_use_id"),
288	            "content": item.get("content", ""),
289	            "is_error": item.get("is_error", False),
290	        }
291	
292	        if flags.show_agents and id_map.get(item.get("tool_use_id")) == "Task":
293	            kept_item = copy.deepcopy(item)
294	            kept_items.append(kept_item)
295	            kept_tool_results.append((kept_item, False))
296	            continue
297	
298	        show_tool, should_shorten = resolve_tool_visibility(
299	            tool_payload, flags.show_tools, id_map
300	        )
301	        if not show_tool:
302	            continue
303	
304	        kept_tool = _shorten_tool_payload(
305	            tool_payload,
306	            should_shorten,
307	            width=flags.shorten_width,
308	        )
309	        kept_item = copy.deepcopy(item)
310	        kept_item["content"] = kept_tool.get("content", "")
311	        kept_items.append(kept_item)
312	        kept_tool_results.append((kept_item, should_shorten))
313	
314	    return kept_items, kept_tool_results

317	def _rewrite_claude_entries(
318	    entries: list[dict],
319	    source_session_id: str,
320	    new_session_id: str,
321	    flags: ConversationFlags,
322	    *,
323	    agent_id_map: dict[str, str] | None = None,
324	    show_message_text: bool,
325	) -> list[dict]:
326	    id_map = _build_claude_tool_name_map(entries)
327	    rewritten_entries: list[dict] = []
328	
329	    for original_entry in entries:
330	        entry = copy.deepcopy(original_entry)
331	        if entry.get("sessionId") == source_session_id:
332	            entry["sessionId"] = new_session_id
333	
334	        entry_type = entry.get("type")
335	        if entry_type == "assistant":
336	            content = entry.get("message", {}).get("content", [])
337	            filtered_content = _filter_claude_assistant_content(
338	                content,
339	                flags,
340	                id_map,
341	                show_message_text=show_message_text,
342	            )
343	            if not filtered_content:
344	                continue
345	            entry["message"]["content"] = filtered_content
346	
347	        elif entry_type == "user":
348	            content = entry.get("message", {}).get("content", [])
349	            filtered_content, kept_tool_results = _filter_claude_user_content(
350	                content, flags, id_map
351	            )
352	            if isinstance(content, str):
353	                if flags.show_user_messages and content:
354	                    entry["message"]["content"] = content
355	                elif kept_tool_results:
356	                    entry["message"]["content"] = [
357	                        tool_result for tool_result, _short in kept_tool_results
358	                    ]
359	                else:
360	                    continue
361	            else:
362	                entry["message"]["content"] = filtered_content
363	
364	            tool_use_result = entry.get("toolUseResult")
365	            if not kept_tool_results:
366	                entry.pop("toolUseResult", None)
367	            elif isinstance(tool_use_result, dict):
368	                should_shorten = kept_tool_results[0][1]
369	                if should_shorten:
370	                    entry["toolUseResult"] = shorten_data(
371	                        tool_use_result,
372	                        width=flags.shorten_width,
373	                    )
374	                if agent_id_map and tool_use_result.get("agentId") in agent_id_map:
375	                    entry["toolUseResult"]["agentId"] = agent_id_map[
376	                        tool_use_result["agentId"]
377	                    ]
378	
379	        if agent_id_map and entry.get("agentId") in agent_id_map:
380	            entry["agentId"] = agent_id_map[entry["agentId"]]
381	
382	        rewritten_entries.append(entry)
383	
384	    return rewritten_entries

420	def _fork_claude_session(source_path: Path, flags: ConversationFlags) -> Path:
421	    source_session_id = get_native_session_id(source_path)
422	    new_session_id, target_path = _generate_unique_session_target(
423	        source_path,
424	        source_session_id,
425	        _generate_claude_session_id,
426	        lambda path, _old_id, new_id: path.with_name(f"{new_id}{path.suffix}"),
427	    )
428	
429	    source_entries = _read_jsonl_entries(source_path)
430	    sidechain_files = (
431	        _find_claude_sidechain_files(source_path, source_session_id)
432	        if flags.show_agents
433	        else []
434	    )
435	    agent_id_map: dict[str, str] = {}
436	    sidechain_targets: list[tuple[Path, list[dict]]] = []
437	
438	    for sidechain_file in sidechain_files:
439	        old_agent_id = _extract_claude_agent_id(sidechain_file)
440	        target_directory = source_path.parent / new_session_id / "subagents"
441	        new_agent_id, sidechain_target = _generate_unique_agent_target(target_directory)
442	        agent_id_map[old_agent_id] = new_agent_id
443	        sidechain_entries = _rewrite_claude_entries(
444	            _read_jsonl_entries(sidechain_file),
445	            source_session_id,
446	            new_session_id,
447	            flags,
448	            agent_id_map={old_agent_id: new_agent_id},
449	            show_message_text=flags.show_agents,
450	        )
451	        sidechain_targets.append((sidechain_target, sidechain_entries))
452	
453	    main_entries = _rewrite_claude_entries(
454	        source_entries,
455	        source_session_id,
456	        new_session_id,
457	        flags,
458	        agent_id_map=agent_id_map,
459	        show_message_text=flags.show_assistant_messages,
460	    )
461	
462	    _write_jsonl_entries(target_path, main_entries)
463	    for sidechain_target, sidechain_entries in sidechain_targets:
464	        _write_jsonl_entries(sidechain_target, sidechain_entries)
465	
466	    _append_claude_history_entry(target_path, new_session_id)
467	    return target_path

624	def _shorten_codex_serialized_value(value: object, *, width: int = 500) -> object:
625	    if isinstance(value, dict | list):
626	        return shorten_data(value, width=width)
627	    if isinstance(value, str):
628	        stripped = value.strip()
629	        if stripped.startswith(("{", "[")):
630	            try:
631	                parsed = json.loads(stripped)
632	            except json.JSONDecodeError:
633	                return truncate_middle(value, max_len=width)
634	            return json.dumps(shorten_data(parsed, width=width), separators=(",", ":"))
635	        return truncate_middle(value, max_len=width)
636	    return value

content: Complete inventory in hand. I'll rename the shortening API to `max_chars` (parameter), `shorten_max_chars` (flag), `_resolve_short_max_chars` / `_is_valid_short_max_chars_token` (CLI helpers), and fix the user-facing `--short` help text and docstrings — while leaving every genuine display width (`elide_to_width`, `console.width`, panel widths) untouched. Let me run the mechanical identifier renames and check docs in one pass.

content.name: Bash
content.command:
cd /Users/giladbarnea/dev/chats
files=$(fd -e py . src tests)
# A. Global unique-identifier renames (safe: these compounds aren't substrings of display-width names)
perl -i -pe 's/\bshorten_width\b/shorten_max_chars/g; s/\b_resolve_short_width\b/_resolve_short_max_chars/g; s/\b_is_valid_short_width_token\b/_is_valid_short_max_chars_token/g;' $files
# B. forking.py + model.py: every remaining standalone `width` is shortening-context (verified: no console.width in these files)
perl -i -pe 's/\bwidth\b/max_chars/g' src/chats/forking.py src/chats/model.py
echo "=== remaining 'width' in shortening files (expect: utils elide_to_width + cli docstrings/help + test prose) ==="
rg -n "width" src/chats/utils.py src/chats/cli.py src/chats/model.py src/chats/forking.py tests/test_short_cli_args.py tests/test_tool_filter.py
echo; echo "=== docs/markdown mentioning shorten width ==="
rg -ni "shorten_width|optional: width|--short" --type md . 2>/dev/null | head -30

124	`--only-metadata` and `--only-id` require a resolved session/file-backed input. Raw stdin/content has no stable session identity to report.

When combined, the CLI emits a warning, disables the contradictory extras immediately, and continues with the normalized flags. `--only-user --only-assistant` is also warned about; it is allowed to fall through to an empty result naturally.

The attached form is strict: `--short=<value>` must satisfy the same validation or the CLI errors.
129	
130	`--no-user` and `--no-assistant` hide only the regular default text for that role. Explicit extras still work with them. For example, `ch --no-user --tools ...` still shows tool outputs from user turns, and `ch --no-assistant --thinking --tools --agents ...` still shows assistant-side thinking, tools, and agent messages. Claude `isMeta=true` user messages are treated as tool-adjacent protocol noise and stay hidden unless `--tools` is enabled.

Done — committed as `4355163`. The misleading `width` is gone from the shortening context across the whole project, and the full suite passes.

## What changed

I renamed the limit to **`max_chars`** everywhere it means "the `--short` character budget," and left every genuine display width alone:

- **`shorten_data(data, width=…)` → `shorten_data(data, max_chars=…)`**, and its docstring now states the limit is applied *per string leaf* and does **not** bound the object's total size — documenting the Q1 gap right where someone would look.
- **`ConversationFlags.shorten_width` → `shorten_max_chars`**, plus the CLI helpers `_resolve_short_width → _resolve_short_max_chars` and `_is_valid_short_width_token → _is_valid_short_max_chars_token`.
- **User-facing text:** the `--short` help now reads "optional: max characters", and the README shows `[MAX_CHARS]` with "explicit MAX_CHARS must be >7".
- Test identifiers, method names, and prose updated to the truthful term.
- **Untouched:** `elide_to_width`, `console.width`, panel/recorder widths, and "ambiguous-width unicode" — those are real column widths, not the shortening budget.

Nine files, +93/−81, all tests green.

## Why `max_chars` and not `total_size`

I went against your `total_size` suggestion on purpose: for a string it's fine, but for an object `total_size` actively implies an aggregate cap — which is exactly the false belief from your Q1 (the limit is per-leaf; an object with many keys still isn't bounded). `max_chars` names the *unit*, characters, so it can't be misread as columns (like "width") or as a total. For a string it reads as "this string's max chars"; for an object as "each string leaf's max chars" — never key-count or dimensions.

The one place I kept a different name is `truncate_middle(s, max_len=…)`: it only ever takes a string, where `max_len` is already unambiguous and truthful, and it's the leaf primitive `shorten_data` calls. If you'd rather have a single vocabulary there too, say so and I'll fold it into `max_chars`.

Goal: unify and truthfully name the chats project's shortening logic. Both pieces are committed and the full suite passes: tools now shorten at the source via one mechanism, and the misleading "width" was renamed to "max_chars". Next action: none pending, awaiting your direction.

## Why delegate at all?

The main agent already holds all the context, so why not just do the work directly? Context management. Both sub-agents and teams spin up a *fresh* context window and hand back only the bottom line, sparing you the token-heavy process that produced it. Two payoffs: (1) you reach the crux of the problem with plenty of headroom left in your own context window, instead of arriving running on fumes; and (2) you escape your own accrued bias.

The flip side: if none of these payoffs apply, don't delegate. The anti-pattern is the user asking for something straightforward and the main agent handing the *whole* task to another agent, ending the session: no context-window hygiene, no synergy, no parallelism, no bias mitigation, just duplicated tokens and a game of broken telephone.

Classic use cases — *generalize* the principles, this isn't a comprehensive list:
- **Exploration** — one sub-agent for a single domain, or parallel sub-agents when your can fan the scope out. Keeps your own context light, and parallel agents save wall-clock time too.
- **Debating the best plan** — an adversarial team handed the user's goal at large plus the exploration results. Synergistic judgement, and it mitigates any single teammate's bias.
- **Reviewing an implementation** — a sub-agent handed the user's goal at large, the exploration results, the finalized plan, and the implementation's commit SHA. Mitigates the main agent's bias toward its own work.

---

1. Orient the agent to the project: the user has mostly likely told you to load a context-gathering skill first thing in the session. Tell the AI agent to load the same skill, with the same arguments the user has specified. On top of that, if throughout the session, you have created, read or edited additional files that are not referenced by the skill, reference them too.  

2. Be generous in giving the agent wider context—understanding *why* it's performing the task will boost its performance. Don't micromanage or over-instruct it. The agent already has the same system prompt as you do out of the box (e.g. `CLAUDE.md` or `AGENTS.md`). It is essentially an equivalent instantiation of yourself. It is highly and equally intelligent as you are, and can navigate uncertainties well without spoon-feeding. Avoid prescribing instructions, giving "how-to" examples, providing examples as to what to think about, or dictating which files, symbols, or paths to look at; avoid any form of providing hints for possible answers for your own queries — this is circular and useless. Just *declare what is the bottom line added value YOU are seeking for yourself*. Instead of specifying which steps to take (dictating the "how" is bad), share only why it was dispatched with it and what you hope to gain. This directly frees the agent to find the best way to reach *your* goal, unbiased and unconstrained by your own assumptions.
    Essentially, all the “Don’ts” above over-fit the agent.
    <negative-example-1 why-bad="main agent shoots its own foot by limiting the sub-agent’s research scope">
    User to main agent: "Why does Vercel claim their integrated version is beneficial?"
    Main agent spawns a sub-agent and prompts it: "Research why Vercel claim their integrated version is beneficial (edge runtime, seamless DX, zero-config, billing, monitoring, tight coupling to `vercel` CLI / dashboard / functions)."
    </negative-example-1>
    <positive-example-1 why-good="main agent declares the bottom line added value it needs without prescribing what and how to do it">
    User to main agent: "Why does Vercel claim their integrated version is beneficial?"
    Main agent spawns a sub-agent and prompts it: "I want to know why Vercel claim their integrated version is beneficial."
    </positive-example-1>
